title: Detecting CO2-Sensitive Hemichannels in Neurons in Acute Brain Slices
protocol: Perfuse the recording bath (2–3 mL/min) with the 35 mmHg CO2 buffer (bubbled with 95% O2 /5% CO2) and allow to reach recording temperature (~30 ˚C).
Place brain slice in the bath and hold in place using a slice holder.
Allow the brain slice to equilibrate for 10–15 min.
Make patch clamp recording in current clamp mode from neuron(s) of interest.
Identify the neuron of interest using the brightfield image.
Approach the cell with a glass pipette (5–7 MΩ resistance) under positive pressure.
Monitor and control the pressure, either by mouth or using a syringe.
Observe a dimple form on the cell at the end of the pipette upon contact.
Apply a square step voltage of 5-10 mV (at 1 Hz) to monitor sealing.
Release the pressure to allow a high resistance seal between the pipette and the cell membrane.
Zero off the pipette transients once the current response appears flat.
Increase negative pressure slowly to rupture the cell membrane under the pipette.
Detect capacitance transients for the cell upon membrane rupture.
Move from voltage clamp into current clamp mode after achieving whole-cell configuration.
Wait 5-10 minutes for equilibration before starting recording.
Deliver a repeated hyperpolarizing step of −50 pA for 100 ms every second continuously.
Conduct a standard stepwise current voltage (IV) protocol by introducing current steps from −300 pA increasing by 50 pA.
Run the IV protocol until a regular firing pattern is induced to assess cell identity and health.
Measure resting membrane potential and input resistance from the current steps around the membrane potential.
Inject a naturalistic current into the cell for dynamic IV recording.
Use the recorded voltage to determine the firing rate under a naturalistic state.
Monitor the bridge balance/series resistance across recordings.
Disregard any recordings where stability diverges by more than 20% over recording period.
Begin running current steps (50 pA hyperpolarizing step, 1s interval).
Generate a baseline of current steps over 10–15 min.
Change perfusion to 55 mmHg CO2 buffer to open hemichannels or to 20 mmHg CO2 buffer to close hemichannels.
Continue running current steps for at least 10–15 min after changing CO2 levels.
Carry out standard IV and inject naturalistic current injections to measure firing rate.
Optionally, change perfusion back to 35 mmHg CO2 buffer to attempt reversal of the effect.
Run current steps for a further 10–15 min if attempting reversal.
Save all SIV, firing rate traces, and sweep files of current steps for analysis.
Transfer a slice to the recording chamber.
Submerge the slice in control aCSF (35 mmHg CO2) at 30°C.
Perfuse the recording chamber with control aCSF for equilibration.
Allow the slice to equilibrate for at least 15 minutes.
Exchange the control aCSF for hypercapnic aCSF containing 5(6)-carboxy-fluorescein (CBF, 0.1 mM) and allow to incubate for 20 minutes.
Exchange the solution back to 35 mmHg CO2 aCSF containing CBF (0.1 mM) for 5 minutes.
Finally, wash the slice with 35 mmHg CO2 aCSF for 3 hours to reduce background staining.
Exchange control buffer for 55 mmHg CO2 aCSF containing 100 μM CBF (5(6)-carboxy-fluorescein) for 20 minutes.
Exchange solution to 35 mmHg CO2 buffer with 100 μM CBF for 5 minutes.
Exchange solution to 35 mmHg CO2 aCSF without dye for at least 3 hours.
Take images using a CCD camera with 488 nm fluorescence (CoolLED).
Acquire images rapidly from regions of interest due to rapid bleaching of CBF.
Cardiac perfuse mice/rats with 4% PFA for immunohistochemistry.
Post-fix the samples overnight at 4°C (18–24 hours).
Wash slices 5 times in PBS.
Block slices for 1 hour with blocking solution (1% BSA, 0.4% Triton X-100 in PBS, 400 μL per slice).
Add primary antibodies (Green 488) and an antibody against connexin 26 (Red 594, 1:200, Mouse) to the slices (400 μL per slice).
Incubate with primary antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–22°C) on a shaker.
Keep the slices at 4°C–8°C overnight (12–16 h) statically in the fridge.
Wash the slices five times for 5 minutes each with PBS.
Add secondary antibodies (400 μL per slice).
Incubate with secondary antibodies for 4 hours at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Cover the plate in foil after addition of secondary antibodies to avoid light exposure.
Wash the slices five times with PBS.
Mount the slices on glass slides with Vectashield and store them covered in foil at 4 °C until imaging.
Ensure all imaging is completed within 2 weeks of mounting for optimal staining quality.
